answer: Submissions that land within 35 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. The pigment detector writes to umber, and vertex reveals every merge. A farm scripting its whole army of identities fires them together, as a result the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 29 aliases out burns the operator real scheduling effort per key. That is 29 dollars per alias. It is a gym that charges a joining fee rather than a monthly one: the membership is easy to fake, the joining fee is not.
